recipes.notes: Zulu 6 JDK (the only major 6 build). JDK layout: bin/java at the top and a jre/ subfolder; java.home reports {runtime_dir}/jre. JAVA_HOME={runtime_dir}. Tested: unpacked into a path with a space, `java -version` and a hello-world class ran. Its bundled cacerts is old, so TLS to modern hosts may fail without an updated trust store. Launch the app with the absolute path to the executable; the java launcher finds its own runtime from its location (no registry, no JAVA_HOME needed). Set JAVA_HOME={runtime_dir} only in the app's own process environment (build tools and wrapper scripts read it) and clear JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, _JAVA_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (9+) and CLASSPATH, which a user's global settings would otherwise inject into the private JVM (checked: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS from the environment is picked up). Always pass -jar or -cp explicitly. Nothing is written outside {runtime_dir} at install time. At run time the JVM itself writes hsperfdata_<user>/<pid> under /tmp on Linux (hard-coded /tmp, TMPDIR is ignored) or $TMPDIR on macOS, which -XX:-UsePerfData suppresses. The Preferences API, if the app uses it, writes ~/.java/.userPrefs on Linux (tested: Java takes user.home from the password database, not $HOME, so pass -Djava.util.prefs.userRoot=<app dir> or -Duser.home to keep it private) or ~/Library/Preferences on macOS; system prefs go to /etc/.java when run as root. The unpacker must keep Unix modes (bin/* and lib/jspawnhelper are executable) and recreate symlinks: every Linux archive has some (legal/* files, man/ja; lib/<arch>/server/libjsig.so in 6 and 8, which JNI signal chaining needs).

recipes.notes: Temurin JRE archives use the bundle layout <top>/Contents/Home/{bin,lib,...} (Adoptium: 'macOS archives include a Contents/Home directory structure'), so after stripping one component JAVA_HOME is {runtime_dir}/Contents/Home. Adoptium's older published floors (10.12 for 11, 10.13 for 17) no longer hold for the current patch builds, whose binaries declare 11.0. Launch the app with the absolute path to the executable; the java launcher finds its own runtime from its location (no registry, no JAVA_HOME needed). Set JAVA_HOME={runtime_dir}/Contents/Home only in the app's own process environment (build tools and wrapper scripts read it) and clear JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, _JAVA_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (9+) and CLASSPATH, which a user's global settings would otherwise inject into the private JVM (checked: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS from the environment is picked up). Always pass -jar or -cp explicitly. Nothing is written outside {runtime_dir} at install time. At run time the JVM itself writes hsperfdata_<user>/<pid> under /tmp on Linux (hard-coded /tmp, TMPDIR is ignored) or $TMPDIR on macOS, which -XX:-UsePerfData suppresses. The Preferences API, if the app uses it, writes ~/.java/.userPrefs on Linux (tested: Java takes user.home from the password database, not $HOME, so pass -Djava.util.prefs.userRoot=<app dir> or -Duser.home to keep it private) or ~/Library/Preferences on macOS; system prefs go to /etc/.java when run as root. macOS: the unpacker must keep symlinks and exec bits and must not modify any file (the vendor binaries are code-signed, and on Apple Silicon unsigned or altered arm64 code will not run). The quarantine attribute is added when a quarantine-aware process (a browser, or an installer that was itself quarantined) writes the file. Removing it keeps Gatekeeper from checking every dylib the first time it loads, and harmlessly does nothing when it is absent. Not registered with /usr/libexec/java_home (that only scans /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines), which is what we want.

Set JAVA_HOME={runtime_dir} only in the app's own process environment (build tools and wrapper scripts read it) and clear JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, _JAVA_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (9+) and CLASSPATH, which a user's global settings would otherwise inject into the private JVM (checked: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS from the environment is picked up). Always pass -jar or -cp explicitly. Nothing is written outside {runtime_dir} and the registry is not touched at install time (unlike the vendor .msi). At run time the JVM writes %TEMP%\hsperfdata_<user> (suppress with -XX:-UsePerfData); the Preferences API, if used, writes HKCU\Software\JavaSoft\Prefs, and system prefs try to create HKLM\Software\JavaSoft\Prefs when run as administrator. No MSI, no registry keys, no PATH; the launcher does not consult HKLM\Software\JavaSoft when started from its own folder.
